items.stem: IFRS 18 primarily standardises which aspect of financial reporting?

options.text: The presentation and structure of the primary financial statements
options.rationale: Correct: IFRS 18 focuses on presentation and disclosure, not measurement.
Revenue measurement is addressed by a different standard.
Deferred tax calculation is outside IFRS 18's focus.
Intangible measurement is governed by other standards.

items.explanation: Correct: IFRS 18 standardises presentation and structure of the financial statements.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO requirements apply when an entity presents a management-defined performance measure (MPM)? (Select TWO)

options.text: Reconcile the MPM to the most comparable IFRS-defined subtotal
options.rationale: Correct: IFRS 18 requires a reconciliation to the nearest IFRS subtotal.

options.text: Explain why the measure provides useful information
options.rationale: Correct: the entity must explain the usefulness of the MPM.

options.text: Present the MPM instead of the IFRS subtotals
options.rationale: MPMs supplement, not replace, IFRS subtotals.

options.text: Keep the MPM undisclosed in the notes
options.rationale: MPMs must be disclosed and reconciled, not hidden.

items.explanation: Correct: an MPM must be reconciled to the nearest IFRS subtotal and its usefulness explained.

items.stem: Interest expense on borrowings is classified in which IFRS 18 income-statement category?

options.rationale: Correct: interest on borrowings falls in the financing category.
Financing costs are not operating items under IFRS 18.
Investing covers returns on investments, not borrowing costs.

options.text: It is excluded from the income statement
options.rationale: Interest expense is presented, within financing.

items.explanation: Correct: interest on borrowings is a financing-category item under IFRS 18.
